intro_html: The closest match to roughened roast potatoes, adapted for a deep fryer. Two trips into the oil: 130 °C, then 185 °C. The simmer is a separate cooking stage. Slender wedges give more crust per bite than whole baby potatoes. This is a source-informed home adaptation, not a kitchen-tested recipe. For a light batter shell instead, see potato wedge tempura.

notes.html:
• The shake roughens softened potato; it does not create new starch.
  • Baking soda makes the cooking water alkaline and helps the outer potato break down.
  • For more roughness, add only ⅛ tsp (about 0.6 g) ordinary baking soda to the original 2 litres of water, before the potatoes.
  • Start checking at 4–5 minutes and shake even less.
  • Do not use baking powder or baked baking soda.
  • For a first batch, skip it: slender floury wedges roughen readily and are easier to handle without it.

• Floury mature potatoes give the fluffy centre you want.
  • Waxy baby potatoes stay creamier and denser.
  • A count of six wedges only works for medium potatoes: measure the cut face.
  • This timing is for 15 mm wedges; 10 mm pieces cook faster and 20 mm pieces need a longer simmer.
  • Test tenderness rather than borrowing the same times.
notes.title_html: Why these potatoes and this cut

notes.html:
• Oregano, basil, garlic powder and pepper go on after the final fry so they keep their flavour without scorching in hot oil.
  • Keep sauces beside the potatoes to preserve the crust.
  • For make-ahead cooking, refrigerate the cooled first-fried wedges, covered once cold, and use within 24 hours.
  • Uncover and check they are surface-dry before the final fry.

• Soft or greasy crust: dry the potatoes more thoroughly, fry smaller batches and let the oil recover before each load.
  • A hard centre means the simmer was too short; it should already be tender before frying.
  • Broken wedges mean too much boiling, soda or shaking: reduce one of those next time.
  • Serve uncovered on a rack rather than piling hot wedges into a bowl.
  • If an electric fryer cannot hold 130 °C, use a tall pot and thermometer for the first fry; do not keep the same timing at an arbitrarily hotter setting.

steps.body_html: • Use Russet, Maris Piper, King Edward or another floury frying potato. Peel and cut lengthwise into 6 wedges per medium potato; cut a large one into 8. Aim for 15 mm at the thickest part, not a fixed number of pieces. Split any wedge wider than 20 mm. Rinse once.
steps.title: Cut slender wedges

steps.body_html: • Bring the water and simmering salt to a boil. Add the wedges, return to a gentle simmer, then cook about 7–10 minutes. Start checking at 6 minutes: a thin knife should enter the thickest centre easily, while the wedge still lifts intact. Tenderness decides when to drain.
steps.time: 7–10 min after returning to a simmer
steps.time_html: 7–10 min after returning to a simmer
steps.title: Simmer until just tender

steps.body_html:
• Drain thoroughly; do not rinse. Return to the empty warm pan, leave uncovered for 2 minutes, then give 2–3 gentle shakes. Stop as soon as the cut faces look lightly scuffed. Do not beat them into mash.
  • Spread on a rack in one layer. Let steam escape for 10 minutes, then refrigerate uncovered for about 30 minutes, until cool, firm and dry on the surface. Dryness is essential; no water droplets should remain.
steps.title: Drain, lightly roughen and dry

steps.body_html:
• Use refined sunflower, rapeseed/canola or peanut oil. In an electric fryer follow its minimum and maximum fill lines. In a pot use about 5 cm depth and fill no more than one third. Fry roughly 150–200 g at a time in a 3-litre fryer, less in a small pot; wedges need room. Restore the stated temperature between batches. Surface water must be gone before any potato enters oil.
  • Heat oil to 130 °C. Lower dry wedges gently and fry for 5–7 minutes per batch, until a thin crust sets but the potatoes stay pale. Move carefully; the first crust is fragile.
  • Drain separately on the rack. Let each batch stop steaming, then chill uncovered for 20–30 minutes, until cool and firm. Complete this first fry for all batches before the final fry.

heat.label: 130 °C oil
heat.label_html: 130 °C oil

steps.title: First fry; cool again

steps.body_html: • Raise the oil to 185 °C. Fry the cooled wedges in small batches for about 3–5 minutes, turning gently, until golden with a rigid crisp surface. Stop at golden rather than dark brown. Drain on a rack for 30–60 seconds.

heat.label: 185 °C oil
heat.label_html: 185 °C oil

steps.title: Second fry until golden

steps.body_html: • Mix the finishing salt, oregano, basil, garlic powder and pepper; crush the herbs between your fingers. Toss with the hot drained wedges, taste, then adjust the salt. Serve immediately with optional mayonnaise on the side. Keep the wedges uncovered and avoid piling them deeply.
steps.title: Season and eat immediately
